nodes.label: Answer only from graph contents - no hallucination
nodes.norm_label: answer only from graph contents - no hallucination
nodes.rationale: Traversal answers must use only what the subgraph output contains and quote source_location when citing a fact; if the graph lacks enough information the agent must say so rather than hallucinate edges.

nodes.label: Constrained query expansion step
nodes.rationale: graphify query's matcher does case-folded substring + IDF only - no stemming, no synonyms, no cross-language match - so a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's node-label vocabulary collapses results to zero; expanding the query against the graph's own extracted vocabulary first (without inventing tokens) fixes this.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS if unsure), never skip the corpus-size warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion scores behind symbols, never run HTML viz on >5000 nodes without warning - keeps graph output auditable and trustworthy.

nodes.label: graphify.serve MCP stdio server
nodes.rationale: Claude Desktop can't run $(...) shell substitution and uv tool installs break system python3's ability to import graphify, so the MCP server command must use the absolute interpreter path printed by cat graphify-out/.graphify_python.

nodes.label: Confidence score rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete confidence values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) are specified instead of a continuous range because production data showed models collapse continuous 0-1 guidance into a bimodal distribution (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+); a fixed rubric is easier for models to follow consistently.

nodes.label: Node ID format rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must use the full repo-relative path (every directory level, not just immediate parent) so semantic-extraction IDs match the AST extractor's scheme; otherwise same-named files in different directories collide and re-extracting an old immediate-parent-format project creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes.

nodes.label: Channels CRUD User Stories
nodes.rationale: Channel operations live entirely on /servers/:serverId: any member can create a channel, all members can view the server's channel list to navigate into a channel's message feed, members can rename channels they belong to, but only the server owner can delete a channel — mirroring the server-level CRUD pattern while tightening delete permission to ownership.

nodes.label: Chat CRUD User Stories
nodes.rationale: Chat stories describe the same online-user messaging capability as Messages but framed as 'chat threads': from / or /servers/:serverId a user clicks an online user to start a chat, views chat threads they belong to, and can edit or delete a message they sent in a chat — largely duplicating the direct-messaging flow already described under Messages.

nodes.label: Messages CRUD User Stories
nodes.rationale: Messaging spans two contexts: from / a user picks a friend/online user to start a direct message thread, and from /servers/:serverId a user posts into the selected channel's message feed. Users can view their message threads (from /) or a channel's messages (from /servers/:serverId), and can edit or delete messages they authored to fix typos or retract content.

nodes.label: Servers CRUD User Stories
nodes.rationale: Logged-in users see their team servers in a sidebar from /, select one to reach /servers/:serverId and read its description/channels/messages, create new servers via a modal form reachable from either / or /servers/:serverId, update the info of servers they own, and delete owned servers — deletion explicitly cascades to all associated channels and messages so no orphaned data is left behind.

nodes.label: Demo User Feature
nodes.rationale: A clearly visible Demo User button appears on both /signup and /login so an unregistered visitor can log in as a guest and exercise the site's features/functionality without first creating an account or entering credentials.

nodes.label: Users User Stories
nodes.rationale: Covers sign-up, log-in, demo-user guest access, and log-out. Successful sign-up/login auto-authenticates the user; invalid submissions surface field-level validation errors while repopulating all previously-valid entries except the password, so users are not forced to redo correct work. Log-out redirects to a page displaying APIs, framed as a way to keep account information secure.
